title: Live Discovery IR
description: The live scan's record of the running EKS estate (STATE_DISCOVERY_LIVE, discovery_livescan_0), written to platform/discovery/live/live_discovery.json with one CSV per table beside it. Code-authored end to end — the AWS cloud-plane walk (aws_live), one in-cluster walk per reachable cluster (k8s_live), the IRSA join between them — so the structure the walk owns is closed here: the cluster record, the in-cluster sections, and the reduced records the walk derives (nodes, IRSA bindings, counts). The objects inside those sections stay open: a Deployment's spec is Kubernetes' contract, not this one's. Every one of them is projected (projection.project): its structure and an allowlist of structural strings — names and references, images, classes, ports, drivers, scheduling contracts — with every other string value replaced by the `<omitted>` marker, so no free-form value a customer authored is in this record: what survives is an identifier, a reference, an enumeration, a scheduling or routing contract (a taint or toleration with key, value and effect; a hostname; a route path), a well-known platform label, a class/mode annotation or a StorageClass provisioning parameter. The AWS-side tag and label maps are key names with the same marker; a security group's free-text description is not recorded. One invariant is stated outright rather than left to code: a Secret record admits the marker under data/stringData and nothing else. Partial results are the contract — an unreachable cluster keeps its AWS-side record with kubernetes_error and no kubernetes section, and every omission is a note — so almost every leaf is nullable and only the identity fields are required.

live_ir_version.description: Bumped with any change to this shape (live_discovery.LIVE_IR_VERSION); unrelated to the platform DAG version.

regions.description: The regions whose EKS clusters were listed, in the order named. A named region that could not be listed is in summary.regions_unreachable and a note; a scan in which no region listed is refused by the tool and never written.

notes.description: Every coverage gap the walk recorded, top-level and per-cluster (prefixed 'cluster <name>: '). Relayed verbatim to the operator.

scanned_by.description: The AWS caller identity ARN the scan ran as (stamped by the tool, absent in the engine's own output).

regions_scanned.description: Regions whose clusters were listed — the length of regions, not the number the operator named.

regions_unreachable.description: Named regions that could not be listed; each is also a note.

string_map.description: Free-form customer text (tags, labels): key names only, every value the `<omitted>` marker (projection.keys_only).

configmap_record.description: A ConfigMap projected like every object: its key names under data/binaryData, each with the `<omitted>` marker as its value and nothing else.

manifest.description: A projected Kubernetes object (projection.project): status and runtime metadata dropped, the applied-configuration annotation dropped, apiVersion/kind stamped, and every string value outside the structural allowlist — a custom label or annotation value, an env literal, a command token, a probe path, a header match, a ConfigMap value — replaced by the `<omitted>` marker, while the route paths, taints, selectors and exact-key platform labels, annotations and StorageClass parameters a migration reproduces are kept. Open beyond its identity: the shape is Kubernetes' contract.

secret_record.description: A Secret projected like every object: its name, namespace, type and the key names under data/stringData, each with the `<omitted>` marker as its value — a member it still carries admits the marker and nothing else. Service-account tokens and Helm release secrets are skipped and counted in skipped_secrets instead.

irsa_role.description: The AWS side of an IRSA binding (aws_live.resolve_irsa_roles): whether the role still exists, whom its trust policy admits, what it grants. exists true carries the detail; exists false with error means IAM says the role is gone (the annotation dangles); exists null with error means the role could not be read — GetRole denied, the role in another account than the clusters, or the annotation not an IAM role ARN at all. All three are migration findings, not scan failures.

irsa_binding.description: A ServiceAccount carrying the eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn annotation. `role` is attached when AWS IAM could be read; absent, the binding stands on the annotation alone.

sa.description: The ServiceAccount's name — named for what it is, so a row never reads as the role's name.

node.description: A live node reduced to the fields that shape capacity (k8s_live._nodes) — never a full Node manifest.

kubernetes.description: One cluster's in-cluster walk (k8s_live.discover_cluster). Namespaced sections respect the walk's namespace scope; cluster-scoped ones (nodes, PVs, StorageClasses, IngressClasses, Karpenter and Gateway API classes, the Namespace list) never do.

configmaps.description: Projected: key names under data/binaryData with every value the `<omitted>` marker. Helm's configmap-driver release records (sh.helm.release.v1.*) are skipped and counted in skipped_configmaps.

skipped_secrets.description: Secrets left out by type, counted: service_account_tokens, helm_releases.

skipped_configmaps.description: ConfigMaps left out by kind, counted: helm_releases (Helm's configmap storage driver).

external_secrets.description: Values held outside the cluster (External Secrets Operator, Secrets Store CSI): store names and the remote object names spelled as fields (remoteRef.key, a secretObjects entry's objectName), never a resolved value; the Secrets Store CSI parameters.objects YAML is a free-form string and is the marker.

bare_pods.description: Pods with no ownerReferences — invisible to any controller inventory.

images_running.description: Every image a pod in scope actually runs — the drift signal against what the workloads declare.

running_instances.description: Live instance count — the one number the nodegroup's scaling intent cannot give.

group_name.description: An identifier; the group's free-text description is not recorded.

network.description: The cluster VPC's layout. Route tables are deliberately a count and ids only: GKE's topology comes from subnet IP allocation and Cloud NAT, so their contents inform nothing the translation generates.

load_balancer.description: An ALB/NLB the AWS Load Balancer Controller created for this cluster, attributed by its controller tag.

ingress_group.description: The ingress.k8s.aws/stack tag — which Ingress group owns it.

service.description: The kubernetes.io/service-name tag — which LoadBalancer Service owns it.

cluster.description: One EKS cluster: its AWS-side record (aws_live) and, when the control plane answered, its in-cluster walk under `kubernetes`. When it did not, `kubernetes_error` says why and `kubernetes` is absent — the AWS-side record stands either way.

certificate_authority_data.description: The public CA bundle (base64), as `aws eks describe-cluster` returns it; needed to reach the endpoint, not a secret.
